title: FORGIVEN FOR ANY OF THE THINGS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And as a penalty they must bring to the priest, that is, to the LORD, their guilt offering, a ram from the flock, one without defect and of the proper value. In this way the priest will make atonement for them before the LORD, and they will be forgiven for any of the things they did that made them guilty.'" - Lev 6:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Any of the things they did.

After a list of thefts, lies, extortions, and false oaths, God gathers them all up in one phrase and pronounces them forgiven.

This is the mercy that runs underneath the whole book. Leviticus is often read as a catalogue of demands, but look at what it keeps doing. It names sin honestly, insists on real repair, and then declares full forgiveness. Nothing swept aside, and nothing held over the person's head.

Notice too the small parenthesis: to the priest, that is, to the LORD. Bringing the offering to a man in a linen tunic was bringing it to God. The priest was not a substitute for God's involvement; he was the appointed point of contact with a God who was really there.

We have a better Priest now, and He is God Himself in our flesh. Because Jesus lives forever, he has a permanent priesthood. Therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through him (Heb 7:24-25).

Completely. Not partially. Not the sins you remember to list. Any of the things you did.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something I have never quite believed God would forgive?
2. What does it mean to me that Christ saves "completely"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for a forgiveness that covers any of the things I have done. I bring them to You through Christ, my great High Priest. Amen.
